spec.title: Accepted requests per second (202/s)
spec.description: Max accepted rps per cell. In 'over' phases (6000 req/s offered) this is the capacity: I expect it to fall as idx goes 0 -> 1 -> 3 -> 5. In 'under' phases (1500 req/s) every cell should sit at 1500. Surprising: no drop between idx0 and idx1 (Node, not Postgres, may be the limit), or v7 and v4 identical at every level. k6 series are not marked stale after a run, so the last value can linger for minutes. k6_b5_resp_202_total is added by B5 (script.js).

spec.title: Client latency p50 and p99
spec.description: Latency seen by k6. 'under' runs: small and flat; a rise with idx means every row costs more. 'over' runs sit in saturation, so the p50 there is mostly queueing (B3 saw about 0.7 s at 5000 req/s). Surprising: p99 spikes in idx5 only (probably the GIN pending list being flushed).

spec.title: Requests not accepted (%)
spec.description: 100 minus accepted share of all requests, per key and idx. Should be 0 in every run (B3 and B4 saw 0 at this capacity). Above 1 % the run collapsed (pool timeouts), which is a finding, not a plain slowdown.

spec.title: WAL written per second
spec.description: Bytes of WAL generated per second, from pg_stat_wal via infra/scripts/pg-wal-exporter.sh (the postgres-exporter has no WAL volume metric on Postgres 15; the metric is added by B5). 'over' runs: it may stay flat even though rps falls, because each row writes more. Surprising: no difference between idx levels.

spec.title: WAL bytes per accepted row
spec.description: WAL bytes per second divided by accepted rows per second. This is the cleanest number of the experiment: my prediction is about 0.7 KB (idx0), 0.8, 1.0 and 1.25 KB (idx5). It is only valid while a run is going (the ratio is empty or noisy between runs). The exact per-run number is in summary.tsv (wal_B_per_row).

spec.title: Full-page images and WAL records
spec.description: Full-page images per second (a whole 8 KB page is written to WAL the first time a page changes after a checkpoint) and WAL records per accepted row. Random keys (v4) touch more different index pages, so I expect more full-page images for v4 than v7, mostly right after the CHECKPOINT at the start of a run.

spec.title: Table and index size (events)
spec.description: Total size of all indexes and of the table (pg_stat_user_tables_*_size_bytes, label relname). The table is truncated before every run, so this shows how it grows during a run. Per-index sizes are NOT in Prometheus: they are in captures/<testid>.txt and summary.tsv (pk_B_per_row, sec_idx_B_per_row). Surprising: index size smaller than the table at idx5 (a GIN on this payload is expected to be large).

spec.title: Checkpoints
spec.description: Timed checkpoints (checkpoint_timeout, 5 min), requested checkpoints (WAL size reached max_wal_size, or a manual CHECKPOINT like run.sh does before each run) and buffers written by checkpoints. I predict almost nothing inside a run (about 130 MB of WAL per run, much less than max_wal_size 1 GB). A request spike at the start of each run is the manual CHECKPOINT, not a finding.

spec.title: Postgres sessions by wait event
spec.description: Number of sessions per wait event (WALWrite, WALSync, LWLock:WALInsert, IO:DataFileRead, Client). With more WAL per row I expect more sessions in WAL waits. Surprising: many sessions waiting on a lock (this table has no hot row, unlike B4) or on pool/Client only.

spec.title: Buffer cache hit ratio
spec.description: Share of block reads served from shared_buffers (blks_hit / (hit + read)), whole database. On a fresh table everything should be cached (about 99 %+). The pre-loaded probe (2M rows, v4 vs v7) is where I expect the ratio to fall, more for v4.

spec.title: Rows inserted per second (Postgres side)
spec.description: tup_inserted rate of the database, from the postgres-exporter. It should match accepted rps (row audit in summary.tsv checks the totals). It counts heap rows only, not index entries. Surprising: a gap to the k6 accepted rate.

spec.title: CPU busy by pinned group
spec.description: Host CPU busy % of the cores of each pinned group (server, postgres, k6, monitoring; the cpu_* variables hold the core ids). Postgres cores are capped by the container quota (cpus: 2) even though 4 cores are in its cpuset, so about 50 % busy on those four cores already means the quota is used up. Surprising: the server group at 100 % in idx0/idx1 'over' runs (then Node is the limit, not Postgres).

spec.title: Postgres container CPU (cores) and throttling
spec.description: CPU cores used by the Postgres container (from infra/scripts/pg-container-exporter.sh) and seconds per second it was paused by the quota. In 'over' runs I expect it to reach 2 cores with throttling above 0: that is where capacity ends. Surprising: well below 2 cores while rps is already flat (then something else limits).

spec.title: Postgres CPU per accepted row
spec.description: Postgres container CPU seconds per second divided by accepted rows per second, in milliseconds. My prediction: about +12 % per b-tree index and about +36 % for GIN, so it grows with idx in both phases (more clearly in 'under'). Only valid while a run is going.

spec.title: Node process CPU (cores)
spec.description: CPU cores used by the ingest-api process (it is pinned to 2 cores, so the ceiling is 2). Should be roughly the same per request at every idx level (the server does not know about the indexes).

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Iterations k6 could not start because all virtual users were busy. 'under' runs: must be 0 (generator ok). 'over' runs: above 0 is expected when the server is saturated (B3 saw it at 5000 req/s), so in 'over' runs read it together with the k6 CPU in the panel above (keep k6 cores under 70 %).

spec.title: Pool waiting and pool wait p99
spec.description: Requests waiting for a connection of the 25 in the pool (ep_pg_pool_waiting) and the p99 wait. Should be near 0 in 'under' runs. A queue in 'over' runs is the saturation itself.

spec.title: In flight and event-loop delay
spec.description: Requests in flight in the server and the event-loop delay. In 'under' runs the delay should be a few ms. A high delay while Postgres is not at its quota means Node is the bottleneck.

spec.title: Database errors by type
spec.description: 503s turned into errors by cause (pool_timeout, statement timeout ...). Should be empty. Anything here means a run collapsed and its rps is not a clean capacity number.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: what does each index cost in throughput?
2. The mechanism: what do the indexes write?
3. Resource view: where does the CPU go?
4. Validity checks: can I trust the run?
